subject: Kickoff: GWikiMatch as the standard long-document matching eval
body:
Hi Bao,

Kicking off GWikiMatch. The retrieval teams have no shared eval for long-form document matching - everyone measures content similarity between document pairs their own way, so numbers do not compare across teams. GWikiMatch fixes that: candidate pairs generated by label propagation over the English Wikipedia hyperlink graph (edge weights from directed hyperlink counts, each node initialized with its own URL as label), then every candidate pair annotated by 3 human raters with majority vote on a 0/1/2 similarity scale.

Deliverables this window: the dataset hosted internally with a documented eval protocol, two baseline systems scored on it, and adoption by at least two retrieval teams.

Milestones: hosted dataset + protocol by 5/29, baselines by 7/3, adoption review 8/5.

Quentin owns the eval protocol and baselines, Bilal data engineering, Oyin infrastructure. Staffing and any platform asks from you next week?

Anders
